root_idea.summary: The root centers on rejection, aversion, or non-acceptance, opposite to رضى and محبت.
root_idea.development: Its lexical range develops from disliking or being averse to something to the experience of an unwanted burden or externally imposed action, the causative making of something hateful, and qualities or objects viewed as detestable. Classical evidence also preserves specialized extensions involving battle severity and an intractable camel.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Quran-attested Form I verb with a distinct basic aversion meaning.
Quran-attested Form IV verb; the public headword is normalized to the active perfect citation form أَكْرَهَ.
Quran-attested active participle group, presented under its singular citation form كَارِهٌ.
Quran-attested noun كَرْهٌ/كَرْهًا denoting unwillingness or externally imposed action.
Quran-attested noun كُرْهٌ/كُرْهًا with the internally experienced burden or aversion sense.

senses.definition: To dislike, reject, or be averse to something; to hate it.
senses.usage_conditions: The aversion may be instinctive or an evaluative, rational, or religious disapproval. The verb expresses the subject’s aversion and does not by itself establish that the disliked thing is objectively bad.

senses.definition: To make something disliked, disapproved of, or hateful to someone.
senses.usage_conditions: A causative construction in which an object is made an object of aversion for another person.

senses.definition: To compel or force someone to do something against their will.
senses.usage_conditions: The active construction takes the compelled person as object; the passive means to be forced. Quranic contexts include coercion in conduct, speech, or religious profession.

senses.definition: Compulsion or coercion: forcing someone to do what they dislike or would not choose.
senses.usage_conditions: The noun denotes externally imposed compulsion; in لا إكراه في الدين it names the absence or rejection of such coercion.

senses.definition: One who dislikes, rejects, or is unwilling to accept or do something.
senses.usage_conditions: An agentive participle used adjectivally or substantively for a person characterized by aversion or unwillingness.

senses.definition: Against one’s will; under externally imposed compulsion or unwillingly.
senses.usage_conditions: This noun is used adverbially for an action performed without consent, including constructions rendered “by force” or “unwillingly.” Some lexical analyses distinguish this outwardly imposed condition from كُرْه.

senses.definition: An unwanted difficulty, burden, or aversive condition experienced intrinsically.
senses.usage_conditions: It can describe something naturally unwelcome or an experience endured with hardship, yielding renderings such as “hateful” and “with hardship.” A lexical analysis reported for the Quran distinguishes this inward experience from the externally imposed كَرْه, while also recording that the two forms may be treated as equivalent.

senses.definition: Disliked, detestable, or held in aversion.
senses.usage_conditions: A passive participle used substantively for something objectionable or hateful.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To show or express dislike, displeasure, disapproval, discontent, or hatred.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form V construction describing the expression or display of aversion, rather than merely having the feeling.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Displeasing, odious, hateful, or blameworthy; something held in aversion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjective describing a quality judged objectionable or offensive.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Aversion or hatred toward a thing, including a sense that it is unsuitable or uncongenial.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal noun or abstract noun for dislike and lack of suitability.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thing or event that one dislikes, disapproves of, or is reluctant to undertake.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for an object or occurrence of aversion, including an action one dislikes doing; opposed to مَنْشَطٌ in the cited lexical usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An affliction or calamity of fate.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Especially in the plural expression مَكَارِهُ الدَّهْرِ, “the afflictions or calamities of fortune.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: Severity or intensity in battle; of a sword, penetrating force in combat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized classical extension, including the expression ذُو الْكَرِيهَةِ for a sword effective in battle.
A specialized animal term, explained metaphorically as resisting obedience.

Expanded statement of the same Form V meaning.
Abstract noun of aversion and unsuitability.
Noun for a disliked thing or event.

cautions: The distinction between كَرْه and كُرْه is explicitly reported as disputed: one analysis differentiates external compulsion from inwardly experienced aversion or hardship, while another treats the forms as equivalent. The entries preserve the differentiated usage without presenting it as uncontested.

Mufradat records several contextual interpretations of Quranic expressions involving compulsion and willing or unwilling submission. These are interpretive alternatives within the coercion and unwillingness senses, not additional lexical meanings.
